topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning objectives of the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic mutations, genetic predisposition, and environmental risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer development, exploring how intrinsic mutational processes, inherited predisposition, and environmental exposures interact across populations.

topics.label: Role of infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens drive oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how various chemical compounds and radiation cause direct and metabolically activated DNA damage leading to mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, microenvironmental factors, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms that facilitate cancer development, including tumour promotion, inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating exposure risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches to determining carcinogenicity and evaluating human risk.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary of the lecture.
